skill.name: vercel
skill.description: Deploy and manage Vercel projects, domains, environment variables, and local workflows through Vercel CLI command guidance.
skill.summary: Use Vercel CLI commands for deployments, project links, domains, environment variables, teams, and local development.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Vercel CLI command reference, and many static backtick hits are Markdown or read-only command false positives. Real risks remain for commands that deploy, mutate cloud resources, run local project code, or pull environment variables into local files. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Production and destructive Vercel commands lack approval guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation steps before production deploys, project removal, domain changes, environment removal, and team switching.

remediation.issue: Environment variable pull can write secrets to local files.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to protect .env files, avoid committing them, and confirm the target project before pulling environment variables.

remediation.issue: Local dev and build commands can execute project code.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to inspect dependencies and project scripts before running Vercel dev or build commands in an untrusted workspace.

remediation.issue: Target project, team, and domain checks are not required before write operations.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short preflight checklist that verifies Vercel login, team context, project name, domain, and environment before changes.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md includes production deployment, project removal, domain addition, environment removal, and team switching commands without explicit confirmation guidance. These actions can affect live services or account resources if executed in the wrong context.

semantic_findings.title: Local Project Code Execution Through Vercel Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends local dev and build commands that can execute the current project code and dependencies. The file does not warn users to inspect the workspace before running those commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are legitimate Vercel workflows, but dev and build operations commonly run project code in the local environment. This risk is contextual and not fully captured by the generic external command pattern.

content.user_title: Manage Vercel Projects from Your AI Agent
content.value_statement: Vercel work often requires switching between deployment, domain, environment, and team commands. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused CLI reference for common Vercel operations.
actual_capabilities: Shows commands for preview and production Vercel deployments.
Lists commands to inspect deployments and review deployment logs.
Guides project listing, linking, and removal through the Vercel CLI.
Covers domain listing, inspection, and project attachment commands.
Covers environment variable listing, addition, pull, and removal commands.
Includes team switching and Vercel CLI login status commands.
limitations: Does not verify that the Vercel CLI is installed or authenticated.
Does not add approval gates before production or destructive commands.
Does not cover every Vercel CLI option or advanced flag.
Does not manage Vercel through the REST API.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Web Project
use_cases.description: Prepare preview or production deployment steps for a Vercel-hosted web application.

use_cases.title: Review Deployment Health
use_cases.description: Inspect a deployment, check recent deployments, and review logs during incident response.

use_cases.title: Manage Project Configuration
use_cases.description: Find commands for domains, environment variables, teams, and project links.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Deployment Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user wants a basic deployment workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the Vercel CLI steps to deploy this project as a preview deployment. Explain when I should use production instead.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Failed Deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer needs help checking a specific deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect a failed Vercel deployment. Ask for the deployment URL, then suggest the safest commands to check status and logs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Local Development
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer needs to link a project and run it locally.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a safe sequence to link this repository to Vercel, pull project settings, and run local development. Include preflight checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Release
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants a release workflow with safeguards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Vercel release workflow that covers team context, environment variables, domain checks, deployment, log review, and rollback.

output_examples.input: I need to check recent Vercel deployments for this project.
output_examples.output: The assistant would suggest listing recent deployments, selecting the correct deployment, and inspecting details before reviewing logs.

output_examples.input: I want to update a Vercel environment variable.
output_examples.output: The assistant would confirm the project, team, environment, and variable name before suggesting add or remove steps.

output_examples.input: I am ready to deploy this app to production.
output_examples.output: The assistant would verify branch, project, team, environment variables, and domain status before recommending the production deployment command.

best_practices: Confirm the active Vercel project, team, and environment before write operations.
Treat pulled environment files as secrets and keep them out of version control.
Ask for explicit approval before production deploys, project removal, domain changes, or environment removal.
anti_patterns: Running production deploys without checking branch, project, and team context.
Pulling environment variables into a shared workspace without secret handling.
Removing projects, domains, or environment variables based on ambiguous names.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It provides Vercel CLI command guidance for deployments, projects, domains, environment variables, teams, and authentication.

faq.question: Does it deploy automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents CLI workflows. Any command execution depends on the host tool and user approval settings.

faq.question: Does it require the Vercel CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows assume the Vercel CLI is installed and authenticated in the working environment.

faq.question: Can it manage environment variables?
faq.answer: It includes commands to list, add, pull, and remove environment variables. Handle pulled values as secrets.

faq.question: Does it use the Vercel REST API?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on Vercel CLI commands, not API requests or SDK usage.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: Use it with explicit approval steps. Verify team, project, branch, domains, and environment variables before production changes.
